comments.content: The InputStream returned by `file.getContents()` is never closed by the caller in `DBNPathBase.copyInputStream` (it only calls `Files.copy`, which does not close the source stream). This leaks an open stream on the file. Either close it here (e.g. wrap in a `FilterInputStream` whose `close()` closes the underlying stream, or document that the caller must close it) or ensure the consumer closes it. Currently `copyInputStream` does not close the stream, so this is a resource leak.

`copyInputStream` does not close the passed `InputStream`. Since the stream comes from `IFile.getContents()` (an Eclipse `IStorage` stream), it must be closed to release the underlying file handle. Use try-with-resources around the stream, or close it in a finally block after `Files.copy`.

When `resource == null` and the node has no `InputStream` adapter, the code silently `continue`s without any log or user feedback. Previously a missing resource was logged at debug level. Consider logging a debug/warn message when neither adapter is available so silent data loss during copy/move is diagnosable.
